The main text directly uses this name in 畏桓温靣兵, and the Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-058-liu-annotation-002) confirms the identity through the marriage narrative involving 桓温's daughter and 王坦之's son. The candidate evidence from aliases.json also confirms this identification. This is an explicit full-name match with no ambiguity.

assertions.interpretation: Wang Wéndù was serving as Chief Clerk (長史) under Huan Gong at the time of the events described.
During this period, Huan requested Wang's daughter in marriage for his son.
After Wang Wéndù returned home to Lántián (his father Wang Shù), the conversation about the marriage proposal took place.
Even though Wang Wéndù had grown up, his father still held him on his knee, indicating the ongoing affectionate relationship at that time.
At that moment, Wang Wéndù took the opportunity to mention Huan's request for his daughter's hand in marriage.
Wang Shù (Lántián) became furious at this point in the conversation.
Later, Huan's daughter eventually married Wang Wéndù's son, a subsequent outcome after the initial refusal.
The annotation identifies Huan Wen's second daughter, courtesy name Bózi, as the one involved in the marriage.
The Wang family genealogy records that Wéndù's son Kǎi married her, corroborating the later marriage outcome.
